candidates.source_name: KALLXO.com (BIRN Kosova / Internews Kosova anti-corruption reporting platform)
candidates.why_relevant: Kosovo's highest-volume corruption-reporting outlet; runs tag archives for 'e-prokurimi' and 'Bankat ne Kosove', publishes named tender/contract investigations and court-case follow-ups. Directly narrates award irregularities, and separately covers commercial banks and the CBK, so it is the single best cross-section of procurement x banking/payments.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll tag/section archives (e.g. /tag/e-prokurimi/, /tag/bankat-ne-kosove/) plus site search for bank/payment keywords; store URL+date+entities, quote sparingly.

candidates.source_name: BIRN Kosova / Gazeta Jeta ne Kosove
candidates.why_relevant: The long-form investigative arm behind KALLXO; produces multi-month procurement investigations and data-driven pieces including analyses built on commercial banks' public auction notices (foreclosure sales), which is a rare banking-sector data trail.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the 'gjate' (long-read) and 'analize' sections; also monitor balkaninsight.com Kosovo tag for English versions.

candidates.source_name: Prokurimi Hapur / Open Procurement Transparency Portal (OPTP) - Levizja FOL
candidates.why_relevant: Civil-society-run mirror of the government e-Prokurimi data, restructured to expose links between contracting authorities, contractors and money since 2010. Filterable by authority (incl. Central Bank, ministries buying payment/banking services) and by procedure type, so it can surface single-source and negotiated-procedure awards without scraping the official portal.
candidates.legal_status: derived public data; check portal terms before bulk scraping
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Inspect for an API/JSON backend behind the search UI; otherwise paginated scrape filtered by CPV/keyword (banke, pagesa, POS, kartela) and by contracting authority.
candidates.discovered_via_method: en+sq search, snowball from Open Contracting Partnership

candidates.why_relevant: Long-running anti-corruption NGO specialised in public procurement monitoring; implementer of OPTP; publishes recurring 'Monitorimi i Prokurimit Publik' reports naming ministries, contract values and legal violations.

candidates.source_name: Democracy Plus (D+) - procurement & OSHP monitoring
candidates.why_relevant: The only CSO systematically monitoring the Procurement Review Body (OSHP) since 2016; publishes case-level reports on blocked/re-evaluated procedures with euro values, and flags integrity failures in award decisions.

candidates.why_relevant: Searchable civil-society database of Procurement Review Body decisions on bidder complaints - the richest single record of contested awards, incl. who complained about which contract and why. candidates.why_relevant: Investigative magazine specialised in public-contract forensics: has analysed hundreds of tenders worth hundreds of millions of euro, naming beneficial owners and political links. Its archive is a ready-made map of which companies repeatedly win state contracts.

negative_findings.description: No Kosovo watchdog or investigative outlet was found publishing a dedicated investigation into procurement of BANKING or PAYMENT services specifically (e.g. state treasury banking services, card acquiring, POS/ATM supply, payment-system IT contracts).
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in sq, sr and en combining bank/payment terms with tender/procurement terms returned generic banking-sector coverage (bank complaints, bank stability) or generic procurement coverage, but no bank-services award investigation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The watchdog ecosystem is strong on infrastructure, energy and vehicle contracts; banking/payments procurement appears to be an unwatched niche, so this cell will need keyword-level monitoring of raw award data rather than relying on ready-made investigations.

negative_findings.description: Transparency International has no standalone national chapter website for Kosovo; TI-related procurement monitoring surfaces through the Kosovo Democratic Institute (KDI) as national contact.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for a 'Transparency International Kosovo' site returned KDI publications and TI regional/global index references instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection should target kdi-kosova.org rather than looking for a TI-XK domain that likely does not exist.

negative_findings.description: Democracy Plus reports the official OSHP (Procurement Review Body) website has had problems since December 2025, with documents older than six months inaccessible.
negative_findings.result_summary: Reported by D+ and echoed in Kosovo media (Epoka e Re, Aug 2026) as part of a wider public-institution web transparency crisis.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Official appeal-decision provenance is unreliable; the CSO mirror at oshp.dplus.org becomes the de-facto archive of record and should be collected proactively before it too goes stale.

negative_findings.description: Two Serbian-language watchdog domains (newsocialinitiative.org, ngoaktiv.org) were inferred from organisation names in third-party coverage rather than confirmed by a direct fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: Their procurement work is documented via Alternativna and Radio Mitrovica Sever coverage; own sites not opened during this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are the only Serbian-language procurement-monitoring producers found; a wrong domain would silently drop sr-language coverage of the north.

negative_findings.description: No Kosovo-specific document-leak or whistleblower publishing platform (SecureDrop-style) dedicated to procurement documents was identified beyond KALLXO's general corruption-reporting intake.
negative_findings.result_summary: KALLXO functions as the citizen reporting intake; no separate leaked-contract repository surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Underlying contract PDFs will mostly have to come from e-Prokurimi/OPTP or from documents embedded in individual articles.

coverage_gaps.description: Watchdog output on procurement of financial services (bank account/treasury services, card acquiring, payment terminals, core-banking or payment IT) is effectively absent.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Instead of waiting for investigations, run standing keyword queries (banke, sherbime bankare, pagesa, terminale, POS, kartela, platni promet, bankarske usluge) against prokurimihapur.org and the OSHP decisions database, and set alerts on KALLXO/Insajderi.

coverage_gaps.description: Serbian-language watchdog coverage is thin and geographically confined to the four northern municipalities; no sr-language monitoring of central-government or CBK-level contracts was found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Verify NSI and ACDC domains, add KoSSev and Alternativna keyword feeds, and consider machine-translated monitoring of sq sources for sr-speaking coverage of central awards.

coverage_gaps.description: Business-side and think-tank watchdogs (GAP Institute, Riinvest, INDEP, Kosovo Chamber of Commerce, American Chamber of Commerce in Kosovo) were not individually verified in this pass despite plausibly publishing procurement-integrity and access-to-finance analysis.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Dedicated follow-up pass on institutigap.org, riinvestinstitute.org, indep.info, oek-kcc.org and amchamksv.org for procurement and financial-services publications.

coverage_gaps.description: Investigative articles and CSO PDFs are the only surviving record of many contested awards, yet several watchdog sites mix http/https and have unstable URL schemes (cohu.org / preportr.cohu.org observed).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snapshot every collected watchdog URL to a local store and to a public web archive at collection time; record both http and https variants.

coverage_gaps.description: Partisan-leaning outlets (Insajderi, Nacionale, Paparaci) supply the highest volume of single-source-award allegations but the weakest evidentiary standard.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define a two-source rule: any allegation from these outlets must be matched to an OSHP decision, an Auditor General finding, an APK intervention or a KALLXO/Preportr piece before entering the intelligence base.

brief: Kosovo has an unusually dense civil-society procurement-watchdog layer for its size: KALLXO/BIRN and Preportr/Cohu do the document-led investigations, Levizja FOL and Democracy Plus run the two most valuable CSO data assets (the Prokurimi Hapur mirror of e-Prokurimi, and the OSHP appeal-decisions database), KDI benchmarks institutional transparency, and Open Data Kosovo supplies red-flag analytics. Serbian-language watchdog capacity exists but is confined to the four northern municipalities (ACDC, New Social Initiative, relayed by KoSSev and Alternativna), and no sr-language monitoring of central-level awards was found. The critical gap for this run is topical rather than institutional: no watchdog in any language was found investigating procurement of banking or payment services specifically, so the cell should be worked as keyword surveillance over the CSO data portals rather than as a feed of ready-made investigations. Reliability is stratified - CSO reports and the OSHP mirror are citable, while high-volume outlets such as Insajderi, Nacionale and Paparaci should be treated as lead generators requiring corroboration.
